1: Figure 1. Offset between annotated start coordinates and experimentally supported start sites.

(A) Histogram of the offset from the gene 5′ edge to the main EPDnew promoter, one value per gene (n = 16,442). (B) As A, offset from the nearest annotated transcript 5′ end. Bins are 10 nt; the x-axis runs from −500 to +500 nt and offsets outside this range are not drawn; positive values place the EPDnew start site downstream of the annotated coordinate. y-axis, number of genes.
2: Figure 2. Cohorts, family detection and independent promoters.

(A) Number of primary anchors per cohort (C1, C2, C2b, C4, C0), stacked by gene class (protein-coding, non-coding, pseudogene). (B) Fraction of planted copies linked to their source promoter (y) by true identity (x, 100% to 70%), with two controls at the right: shuffled copies and unrelated promoters carrying a 300-nt chunk of the source; n = 300 source promoters per point. (C) Families of two or more loci by family size (x, distinct loci, in six bins): share of families (y) by the gene class of most members (colour) and by arrangement (solid, all loci on one chromosome within 5 Mb; hatched, dispersed); the number of families is given above each bar and four named families (OR7E, GOLGA2/GOLGA6, USP17L, SNAR) below the panel, with USP17L and SNAR in orange. (D) Number of C1 segments and of independent promoters (sum of weights 1/family size) per gene class.
3: Figure 3. Test bench for the positional discovery statistic.

(A) Weighted count per upstream position (−200 to −1 nt) in C1 for the best-scoring k-mer matching each known element (TATA box, CCAAT box, GC box); the shaded band marks the scoring window and the dashed line the expectation from the k-mer's own flanks. (B) Number of planted motifs recovered out of 5 (one per planted position) in round A, by fraction of carrier promoters (x) and positional jitter SD (series). (C) As B for round B (lower fidelity, fewer carriers, larger jitter). (D) k-mers passing FDR ≤ 0.05 in the round-B planted data, classified as matching a planted motif, matching a hit in the unplanted data, or neither. Recovery: k-mer within Hamming distance 1 of the motif, FDR ≤ 0.05, peak within 2 SD + w/2 + 3 nt of the planted position.
4: Figure 4. Detection limits of iterative motif discovery.

(A) Core zone: fraction of planted motifs recovered (colour scale, 0 to 1; n = 3 positions per cell) by number of carrier promoters (rows: 14, 28, 56, 139, 278, 557, 1,392) and by motif fidelity and positional jitter (columns: fidelity 0.75, 0.85, 0.95, each at jitter SD 0 and 15 nt). (B) As A for the distal zone (n = 2 positions per cell). (C) Motifs passing FDR ≤ 0.05 in each planted cohort, divided into those matching a planted motif, those matching a motif from the unplanted data, and others. Recovery criterion and FDR as in Methods 2.6.
5: Figure 5. Reproducible promoter elements, their positional profiles and the TATA position.

(A) For each element, its representative position weight matrix (sequence logo; letter height in bits) and its positional profile: observed over expected number of promoters with a match starting at each upstream position (5-nt window), from −200 to −1, in full-length promoters with an EPDnew or CAGE start site, without pseudogenes. Observed counts are family-weighted and count a match on either strand; the expectation is the same scan of ten shuffled cohorts (dinucleotide shuffles within 50-nt blocks), averaged over cohorts and over 51 nt. Blue fill marks a ratio above 1; the scale is given at the left of each row. Triangles mark summits above the cut in panel C (orange, highest summit; light orange, others). The dashed line marks −40. (B) Result of each element in six replicates (independent random seeds): filled square, a motif of the element passes FDR ≤ 0.05; open square, found but above the FDR cut; blank, not found; the number in each square is the best motif score (−log10 P); the next column counts the replicates in which the element passes. A motif belongs to an element when its PWM columns correlate with the representative PWM (mean Pearson r ≥ 0.85 over at least 5 informative columns), in either orientation and at any position. The right column gives the share of matches on the sense strand within 5 nt of the element's main summit, observed and expected from the shuffles (0.50 where the shuffles give fewer than 5 matches); orange marks a binomial P < 0.001; palindromic elements are labelled. (C) Highest summit score (−log10 P, Poisson; log scale) of each element (dots) and of 100 null profiles (ticks), in which each shuffled cohort is compared with the mean of the other nine; the dashed line is the cut, the highest null summit score. (D) Positional profiles (7-nt window) in promoters with a sense-strand TATA motif starting at −37 to −25 (orange) and in all other promoters (blue), each group against the shuffled versions of its own promoters. Grey band, slot A (starts −58 to −46); peach band, the TATA position (starts −37 to −18); dotted line, ratio 1. Family weights as in Methods 2.4.
6: (A) Positional profiles of core-promoter elements in full-length promoters with an EPDnew or CAGE start site (12,084), extended to +100: observed over expected number of promoters with a sense-strand match starting at each position (3-nt window), from −60 to +100; +1 is the start-site base and there is no position 0 (dashed line). Rows show discovered PWMs (TATA box, two Initiator motifs, YY1; match thresholds calibrated as in Methods 2.6) and published consensus sequences matched exactly (TCT, DPE). The expectation is the same count in ten shuffled cohorts (dinucleotide shuffles within 50-nt blocks); the scale is given at the left of each row. (B) As A for the start-codon context and the 5′ splice donor (grey). (C) Published consensus sequences tested at their published start positions (second column): observed over expected family-weighted number of promoters with an exact sense-strand match, with the number of matching promoters in brackets, in all promoters and by group (TATA+ and TATA−: with or without a sense-strand TATA motif starting at −37 to −25; CpG: CpG-island-like over −500 to −1; Inr+: Initiator BBCA+1BW at −3). Shading marks Poisson −log10 P ≥ 3 (dark, ≥ 3-fold; mid, ≥ 1.5-fold; light, < 1.5-fold); beige, not enriched; n, fewer than 5 matching promoters. (D) Genes whose promoters carry the TCT consensus starting at −3 to −1, by class. Family weights as in Methods 2.4.
7: Figure 7. The grammar across cohorts and the architectures it forms.

(A) Elements (rows) passing FDR ≤ 0.05 in each run (columns: C1 Pol II genes, protein-coding, lncRNA, small-RNA genes and pseudogenes; C2; C2b; C3; C4 primary anchors, Pol II genes and small-RNA genes), on sequences from −300 to +100 (+1 is the start-site base; no position 0). Each box gives the start position of the element's best-scoring motif; box area is the number of carrier promoters and shade the fold enrichment (O/E); the number beside a box counts the passing motifs assigned to the element; a dot marks no motif passing. A motif is assigned to an element when its consensus, on either strand, contains the element's core word and its start lies in the element's position range. The rows below give the number of passing motifs per run and, of those not assigned to an element, the number with O/E > 20 and fewer than 150 carriers (orange, more than 5). (B) Promoter architectures in C1 promoters with an EPDnew or CAGE start site, without pseudogenes (12,084 promoters): each node is a set of elements called at their positions (Methods 2.6), placed in rows by the number of elements; node area is the family-weighted number of promoters with exactly that set, and colour the share of them that is CpG-island-like (orange, low; blue, high). Numbers give promoters and, in brackets, the ratio to the same count in shuffled copies of the promoters; dashed outlines mark ratios below 2. Lines join architectures that differ by one element. Architectures carried by fewer than 25 promoters are not drawn; the share of promoters with no element called is given above the tree. Element call rates are in S1 Fig. All runs used the settings of Methods 2.6 with the family weights of Methods 2.4.
8: Figure 8. The motif at −17 and target-site duplications.

(A) Schematic of a copy inserted by LINE-1: the endonuclease target site (TT/AAAA), the duplicated target site (box) upstream of the 5′ edge and downstream of the poly(A) tail, and the gene copy (arrow); not to scale. (B) Fraction of promoters with TTAAAR or TTRAAA starting at −25 to −10 (filled) or in 16-nt background windows starting at −200, −250, −300 and −350 (open, averaged), and with TATAWA starting at −35 to −25 (hatched), by cohort and gene class; RPL/RPS pseudogenes shown separately. (C) Fraction of genes with a target-site duplication (filled) and the same search on flanks from mismatched genes of the same group (open; mean of 5 random pairings), by cohort and gene class. A duplication is an exact repeat of at least 12 nt, not low-complexity (no base above 75% of the repeat), shared by −30 to −1 and +1 to +120 from the 3′ end. (D) As C for pseudogenes with and without the −25 to −10 word of B. (E) Number of pseudogene duplications (y) by the start position of the upstream copy (x, nt before the 5′ edge); the shaded band marks the start of the −17 motif.
S1: S1 Fig. Element calls in real and shuffled promoters.

Family-weighted number of C1 promoters with an EPDnew or CAGE start site, without pseudogenes (12,084), in which each element is called inside its positional zone (bars), and the same count in shuffled copies of the promoters (dinucleotide shuffle within 50-nt blocks over −300 to +100; orange ticks). The percentage gives the share of calls above the shuffled count. Zones and calling rules as in Methods 2.6 (Promoter architectures).
